title: SA/1250/1999 of DAYA SHANKAR JOSHI  and OTHERS Vs THAKURJI  MAHARAJ VIRAJMAN MANDIR  and OTH

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Second Appeal No.1026 of 2001
(Old No.1250 of 1999)
Daya Shankar Joshi & others ...........Appellants
 Versus
Sri Thakurji Maharaj Virajman Mandir & others
 .......Respondents
Shri Sharad Sharma, Senior Advocate assisted by Shri Kamlesh Lohani, learned
counsel for the appellants.
None appeared for the respondents.
Dated: December 13, 2012
Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
 Inspite of sufficient service, no one has put
in appearance on behalf of the respondents.
2. Heard learned counsel for the appellants.
3. Present Second Appeal has been filed by the
appellants against the judgment and order dated
14.09.1999 passed by the Additional District Judge,
Kashipur, district Udham Singh Nagar in Civil Appeal
No.09 of 1999 "Sri Thakurji Maharaj and others Vs.
Daya Shankar Joshi and others", by which the
judgment and order dated 12.01.1999 passed by the
Civil Judge (Junior Division), Kashipur in Original Suit
No.124 of 1987 "Sri Thakurji Maharaj & others Vs.
Daya Shankar Joshi and others" has been set aside
and the suit of the plaintiffs/respondents has been
decreed.

2
4. Plaintiffs/respondents filed Original Suit
No.124 of 1987 "Sri Thakurji Maharaj & Others Vs.
Daya Shankar Joshi and others" against the
appellants, seeking injunction, restraining the
appellants from performing any religious activities and
further an injunction to restrain them from interfering
in the alleged possession of the respondents. The
respondents, in the suit, contended that the property
in question was a religious and charitable trust, which
was created by the grandfather of the respondent no.2,
namely, Shri Tota Ram R/o Mohalla Rehamkhani,
Kashipur and it was contended that he, about 90 years
back, had constructed a temple, chabootara, shops,
well and two storied Dharamshala for public benefit at
large. The respondents contended that at the time,
when Shri Tota Ram created the trust, it was he, who
managed the property and thereafter, the management
of the property was to be taken care of by his
successors i.e. Ram Swaroop and his nephew, whom
the respondents contended were the trustees of the
said trust created by Shri Tota Ram. The plaintiff no.2,
in the suit, contended that the trustship of the
property was to be devolved on the basis of succession,
and in this work of public and religious trust, Shri Tota
Ram was assisted by his son-in-law, who also
contributed in the construction of temple. It is alleged
that according to the respondents, the trust was
managed by one Shri Prem Bihari Lal, who used to
take care of the trust property, till he died in the year
1981. The father of the appellant no.1-Nityanand Joshi
was the Pujari of the temple and he used to perform all

3
religious functions and worship of deities and after his
death, the appellant no.1 is taking care of deities and
temple. The plaintiffs contended that the property in
question stands recorded with the Municipal Board in
khasra nos.170 & 171, in which there exists three
shops and temple Mahadev Thakur Ji, Hanuman Ji
and others. It was the case of the plaintiffs that no one
outside the family could manage the trust. The
respondents contended that in the year 1958, the
second floor of Dharamshala was renovated from the
money, which was contributed by the trust. It is
admitted case, according to the pleadings of the plaint,
that in the municipal records, the aforesaid property is
recorded as Dharmarth Badrinath Trust, as the same
was utilized by the pilgrims, who used to stay on their
way to visit to Badrinath Shrine and the income, which
was received from, was utilized for the maintenance of
the trust property. The plaintiffs placed reliance on a
judgment/order rendered in their suit decided in the
year 1981, whereby the trustees were to be inducted on
the basis of inheritance and on the basis of belonging
to the same family clan. The defendants/appellants put
in appearance and filed written statement and took a
specific plea that the trust was never created by Shri
Tota Ram, as he did not had any resources available
with him to make the investment in creation of trust,
rather in 1987, it was the appellants, who had
renovated the first floor and installed the statues of
deities. The appellants denied Shri Raghunandan
Prasad, as to be the managing trustee of the trust, as
he has no rights. The people of the locality, having faith

4
in the deities installed in the temple, constituted a
registered body, which was registered under the
Societies Registration Act, despite the fact that the
registration and existence of the body, managing the
trust property, was known to the respondents, but has
deliberately not impleaded them as a party. The
specific plea was taken in the written statement that
looking to the pleadings of the plaint, where admittedly
a public and religious trust was created, the suit before
the Civil Judge was not maintainable, as it was barred
under Section 91 read with Section 92 of C.P.C., as the
jurisdiction for adjudication of any dispute in relation
to the trust property is vested with the District Judge
thus, the Civil Judge will not have any jurisdiction to
try the suit. Since the trust, on which the respondents
placed reliance to have been created by Shri Tota Ram,
was never registered nor had any legal existence and,
thus, it will be ousting the jurisdiction of the civil
Court. The appellants had taken a plea that the
plaintiffs have never been in possession, further more,
the plaintiff no.2 was not the family member, as he was
separated from the family, he, being adopted by his
Fufa and thus, his relationship with the family of Shri
Tota Ram stood severed, and in view of the judgment
rendered in 1918, he cannot claim the rights to
manage the trust by succession. The plaintiff no.2
admitted that Nityanand Joshi was appointed as priest
since 1962 and performing the religious functions ever
since then. The learned trial Court framed, as many as,
four issues, for the purposes of the present Second

5
Appeal, the two issues were of relevance, which are
being reproduced below:-
"i) As to whether the plaintiff no.2 is the trustee
of plaintiff no. 1 and has acquired ownership
and right to manage the same, .
ii) As to whether the suit was barred under
Section 91 & 92 of C.P.C."
5. The appellants, in support of their
contention, placed on record the Paper no.26-Ga
certificate of registration by Registrar, Paper no.27- Ga
application given to the Registrar, receipts of the
Municipal Board, copy of the assessment register Paper
no.29-Ga & 30-Ga, the electricity bill, the proceedings
register of the society showing that it was effectively
functioning Paper no.36-Ga-2. The learned trial Court
decided Issue no.1 against the respondent and held
that the defendant no.1 was managing the trust
property, after constituting a registered society, with
the aid of the people of the locality. The trial Court also
held that it has been the pleading of both the sides that
the property is a public religious property, which was
managed by the Badrinath Mandir Evam Dharamshala
Jeernodhar Samiti, which is a registered society. The
trial Court held that it was established by evidence on
record that property is a religious charitable property.
While dealing with the contents of the pleadings in
paragraph no.4 of the plaint, the plaintiffs contended
that in the Municipal Board, the property has been
recorded as "Dharmarth Shri Badrinath", but no such
trust is found to be registered or recorded in the
municipal records, as the same is not recorded in the
said name. The trial Court held that the defendants are

6
managing the property, as a public religious property,
under a valid existing registration and have renovated
the property, installed the deities, and thus, in view of
the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court
reported in A.I.R. 1957 S.C. 797 that for the purposes
of establishment of a religious trust, there is no
necessity to show the existence of a document of title,
which could be presumed from the conduct of parties
and concluded that it was a public religious trust
property. The trial Court, vide its judgment dated
12.01.1999, dismissed the suit, holding that the
plaintiffs have not proved that they are in possession
and managing the property and have failed to prove, by
any evidence, that they had any right over the trust
property. Aggrieved by the said order, the plaintiffs
preferred First Appeal before the learned District
Judge, which was registered as Civil Appeal No.9 of
1999, the same has been allowed by the Additional
District Judge Kashipur, vide judgment dated
14.09.1999, against which the present Second Appeal
has been filed by the appellants.
6. The Second Appeal was admitted before the
Allahabad High Court on 15.10.1999 on the following
substantial questions of law:
(i) Whether the 1st Appellate Court has erred at
law in failing to interpret the provisions
contained under Section 91 and 92 of the
Code of Civil Procedure?
(ii) Whether the defendant/appellant had taken
a specific pleading to the effect that the suit

7
is barred in view of the provisions of
Sections 91 and 92 and the same could be
filed only before the District Judge as
admittedly the property being managed for
the religious and charitable purpose, the
jurisdiction will lie to the District Judge of
the district?
(iii) Whether the impugned judgment and decree
is illegal and based on perverse findings and
deserves to be set aside?
(iv) Whether in view of the facts and
circumstances of the present case the suit
ought to have been dismissed?
 Same day stay application was also
considered and stay order was granted. On steps being
taken in the Second Appeal, the respondents had put
in appearance and filed their counter affidavit, but
thereafter did not participate in the proceedings of the
Second Appeal. The Second Appeal was transferred to
this Court under Section 35 of the Reorganization Act
and thereafter, a fresh notice, as contemplated under
the U.P. Reorganization Act, 2000, was sent to the
respondents, but they have not put in appearance. On
31.07.2008, the respondents were directed to be served
by way of publication, which the appellants did, and an
affidavit of service was filed on 17.02.2009. The Second
Appeal was taken up again on 04.03.2011, on which
day, this Court called for a report from the Registry
and thereafter, by order dated 04.04.2011, this Court
held that the service on the respondents is sufficient.

8
7. Learned Senior Advocate for the appellants
submitted that in addition to substantial questions of
law framed by the Allahabad High Court, the
appellants also pleaded that in absence of there being
any registration of trust, as managed by the
respondents, it could not be said that any valid trust
was in existence in the absence of its registration
under Section 5 of the Indian Trust Act. He submitted
that the appellants specifically took a ground that they
are managing the property of the public religious trust
under a registered deed and byelaws in the name of
"Dharmarth Shri Badrinath Narayan Dharamshala
Jernodhar Samiti" thus, they have got a right to
manage the same. He contended that the defendants
have got a right over the property to manage it as a
registered body, because their registered body stands
recorded in the municipal record and this fact of
registration of society stands admitted by the plaintiffs.
He argued that the Appellate Court erred in law in
failing to reverse the findings of fact recorded by the
trial Court and erroneously substituting its own
finding, which was not even pleaded by the respective
parties in the suit thus, none of the ingredients
essential for the grant of permanent injunction was
made out and thus, the suit has rightly been
dismissed. He also submitted that the plaintiffs since
have failed to prove the establishment of trust by Shri
Tota Ram, this finding has been affirmed by the First
Appellate Court, this affirmation with regards to the
establishment of trust was not proved by the plaintiffs
and both the Courts below have decided against the

9
plaintiffs that they have failed to discharge their
burden to prove the existence of trust. He submitted
that in view of the bar of Section 91 & 92 of C.P.C., in
the presence of the pleadings of the plaintiffs that it
was a religious and charitable trust, the suit, before
the Civil Judge, was not maintainable in the absence of
there being any proceedings under Section 91 & 92 of
C.P.C. Thus, the Second Appeal deserves to be allowed,
as the suit, itself, was not maintainable and since the
respondents having failed to prove the existence of
registered trust created by the forefathers, this finding
stands affirmed by the First Appellate Court and since,
no Second Appeal has been filed by the respondents
against the aforesaid finding, the Second Appeal filed
by the appellants deserves to be allowed.
8. None appeared for the respondents. But,
earlier the respondent no.2 filed counter affidavit to the
stay application and affidavit. In the counter affidavit,
it is submitted that the temple in question is a very old
temple, built for the benefit of the general public. It is
also submitted that the question in dispute, in the
instant case, is regarding the right to manage the Trust
and property relating thereto. It has been specifically
noted by the learned Appellate Court that the dispute
between the parties was not regarding the nature of the
Trust property e.g. whether it was a public or private
trust. It has been noted by the learned Appellate Court
that the only dispute concentrated into the right of
management of the trust property and it has been

10
recorded by the learned Appellate Court that Shri Tota
Ram and, after him, his successor-in-interest were the
Manager of the trust property and were performing all
the acts and duties relating to the trust. Likewise, it
has also not been accepted by the Court below that the
ancestors of the plaintiffs/respondents were not the
trustees of the trust property. The conclusions of the
trial Court to the effect that the plaintiffs or their
ancestors were not trustees of the trust property was
reached at upon an illegal and erroneous analysis of
the evidence available on the record and, therefore,
that finding was not accepted by the Appellate Court
on the ground that the defendants/appellants have
illegally and forcefully thrusted themselves into the
affairs of the management of the trust property. It is
further submitted in the counter affidavit that the
learned Appellate Court has very exhaustively and after
detailed analysis of the evidence of the parties available
on record, both documentary as well as oral, had
drawn a legal and rational inference therefrom to the
effect that the temple and Dharamshala was
established by Shri Tota Ram and that Shri Tota Ram
continued to manage and look after the affairs of the
temple and the property relating thereto throughout
his life and after his death, Shri Ram Swaroop, his son,
and after Shri Ram Swaroop, Shri Prem Behari Lal took
over and managed the affairs of the property in
question. It is also submitted in the counter affidavit
that this is a finding of fact recorded by the last Court
of fact and is not liable to be questioned in the Second
Appeal within the purview of Section 100 of the Code of

11
Civil Procedure. It is also submitted in the counter
affidavit that the Committee had been constituted and
registered only after the institution of the civil suit for
injunction. Therefore, the very advent of the
Committee, its formation as well as its registration may
be regarded as an after-thought and a step engineered
by the defendants/appellants, to intrude into the
property of the trust. It is further submitted that the
appeal does not involve any substantial question of law
and the memo has been presented without precisely
stating the same, as required by Section 100 of the
Code of Civil Procedure. It is also submitted that no
such plea, as bar of Sections 91 and 92 of the Code of
Civil Procedure, were neither raised before the
Appellate Court nor there was any evidence to that
effect and cannot be raised before this Court.
9. I have considered the submission advanced
by the learned counsel for the appellants and have
perused the papers available on record. The
defendants/ appellants in their written statement came
up with the case that the plaintiffs/respondents
themselves admitted in the plaint that disputed
property is public charitable and religious endowment.
The defendants/ appellants also contended in their
written statement that the District Judge has
jurisdiction to hear the suit and the suit is barred by
Section 91 and 92 of C.P.C. The trial Court held that it
has been the pleading of both the sides that the
property in dispute is a public religious property. The

12
trial Court also held that plaintiffs failed to prove that
the plaintiff no.2 is trustee of plaintiff no.1 and has
acquired ownership and right to manage the same. The
trial Court did not decide the issue as to whether the
suit is barred under Section 91 and 92 of C.P.C. Even
this issue has not been discussed by the trial Court.
The trial Court, while deciding the issue no.1, observed
that defendants did not press issue no.2. The learned
lower Appellate Court observed in its judgment that
though it is admitted to both the parties that trust is a
public trust but dispute is in respect of management of
trust. It is true that issue no.2 regarding
maintainability of suit before the Civil Judge was not
pressed during the hearing of the suit, but the said
question goes to very competence of the Court to decide
the issue and since it governs the jurisdiction of the
Court, the trial Court should have decided the issue. I
am satisfied with the argument of learned counsel for
the appellants that in view of the restrictions imposed
by Section 91 and 92 of C.P.C., the trial Court should
have decided this issue as preliminary issue. Infact
both the Courts below erred in law by not discussing
and deciding the issue no.2.
10. In view of above discussion, substantial
question of law nos.1 and 2 are answered in
affirmative. The Second Appeal is allowed. Judgment
and decree dated 14.09.1999 passed by the Additional
District Judge, Kashipur in Civil Appeal no.9 of 1999
"Sri Thakurji Maharaj ji Mandir Mahdev and others Vs.

13
Daya Shankar Joshi and others as well as judgment
and decree dated 12.01.1999 passed by the Civil Judge
(Junior Division), Kashipur in Original Suit No.124 of
1987 Sri Thakurji Maharaj va Shivji Maharaj Mandir &
others Vs. Daya Shankar Joshi and others are
quashed. Matter is remanded back to the Civil Judge
for fresh adjudication. Since matter is sent back for
fresh adjudication, substantial question of law nos.3
and 4 are not answered.
11. No order as to costs.
 (V.K. Bist, J.)
Arpan 13.12.2012
